headline: Inferring interaction networks from indirect relational data across scales
label: Network Inference Across Biological Systems
summary: Recent preprints apply optimal transport, coevolution and Boolean modeling to reconstruct interaction networks from food webs to siderophore systems.
synthesis: The shared thread is reconstruction of interaction structure from indirect relational evidence rather than direct measurement. Optimal-transport alignment of motif-role profiles recovers robust interaction backbones across 129 Sub-Saharan African mammal food webs. Coevolution-driven CIM infers specific siderophore-receptor pairings from uncurated genomes, reconstructing iron scavenging networks across nine bacterial taxa and revealing topological diversity of microbial exploitation. Separately, natural bZIP dimerization interactomes from three species are repurposed as Boolean logic substrates through mass-action modeling and genetic optimization. The novelty lies in transferring network inference methods across ecological, microbial, and molecular scales. The pLM item, which introduces Residue Embedding Diversity as a protein quality metric for metagenomic space, is adjacent rather than network-based.
